judge.confidence_method: self-consistency: share of the samples that gave the majority decision (verbalized numbers kept, not used)

ground_truth.label: human-annotated
ground_truth.meaning: real items labelled by one annotator; annotator error is part of the ground truth
purpose: selective prediction when no option applies: does confidence fall on out-of-scope requests?
caveats: public since 2019: probably in the pretraining data of the judges audited

queries written by crowd workers to a prompt (paraphrase a seed phrase, or answer a scenario, for a given intent; out-of-scope queries crowd-sourced too; Larson et al. 2019), not production traffic; one label per query, no inter-annotator agreement published
label noise not yet measured: a 500-row random sample is drawn for two blind annotators (examples/clinc150/relabel-sample.json)
1900 distinct texts in 1900 rows (case and whitespace ignored)
domains banking, credit_cards only: 900 in-scope test queries, 1000 out-of-scope ones (out of scope for all 150 intents); a draft subset until the pre-registration fixes it
0 of 1900 texts also appear in the train or validation splits (case and whitespace ignored); _meta.text_in_train marks them
